Textual reuse analysis reveals significant parallels within the Pali tradition and across Buddhist narrative literature [DharmaNexus]. The commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, first volume) incorporates extensive stanzas corresponding directly to this apadāna (with 23 matches, particularly segments §0.3–5.4) [DharmaNexus]. The text also shares standard stock stanzas—principally the concluding reflections on the fruits of giving and attainments of arhatship (§4.1–8.1)—with numerous other poems in the *Therāpadāna*, including the *Annasaṁsāvakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 27), the *Paṇṇadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 283), and the *Ārakkhadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 313) [DharmaNexus]. In non-Pali literature, DharmaNexus detects textual reuse alignments between this apadāna and the Sanskrit narrative collection *Kaṭhināvadāna* (notably around segment §4.4) [DharmaNexus].
